newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt settles with Ngai Tahu for NZ$170 mln.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt settles with Ngai Tahu for NZ$170 mln.

text.p: New Zealand Waitangi Treaty Negotiations Minister Doug Graham on Friday announced that the New Zealand goverment had agreed in principle to settle for NZ$170 million in land and cash the outstanding claims of the South Island Maori Ngai Tahu tribe.
"It is intended that the heads of agreement to be signed in Wellington tomorrow morning will lead to a full and final settlement of the claim," Graham said in a statement.
Graham said the settlement would preserve and enhance public access rights, and anxieties private land owners have had would be removed.
The heads of agreement must be ratified by Ngai Tahu beneficiaries by a process and majority acceptable to the incoming government.
A general election will be held on October 12.

The key elements of the settlement are a formal apology from the Crown for breaches of the principles of the Treaty of Waitangi, NZ$170 million in land and cash, and a "relativity clause" similar to that struck last year with the Waikato Tainui tribe.
The clause allows for an increase in the settlement amount if the government lifts its $1 billion cap on all Maori Treaty settlements.

The settlement includes the right of first refusal over Crown land declared surplus currently held by: Timberlands West Coast, Crown Research Institutes, some Crown Health Enterprises land, Landcorp, Transit New Zealand, tertiary education institutes, the fire service, two properties belonging to Southland's The Power Company Ltd, Crown shares in Dunedin and Invercargill airports and the Highbank hydro power station.
The settlement also includes a second right of refusal to the Crown's shares in Christchurch International Airport and first right of refusal over all but the land of Milford airport.

Ngai Tahu will also receive title to the farmable parts of the Greenstone Valley, Elfin Bay and Routeburn high country stations amounting to about 10 percent of their total area subject to public interest covenants.
Title to the Crown Titi (Muttonbird) Islands and Rarotoka (Centre Island) will be vested in Ngai Tahu.
Also included are rights to food and food gathering areas and changes to 78 place names with provision for joint Maori and English names.
The government is committed to settling all Treaty claims by the year 2000. Earlier this week it settled the Whakatohea claim in the North Island's Bay of Plenty for NZ$40 million.
